text.p: These are leading stories in this morning's Paris newspapers.
-- Unemployment - "the elections put a brake on new job hiring". The number of jobseekers rose by 32,400 or 1.1 percent in May from April, rate remains unchanged at 12.5 percent.
-- Bank of France study expects 2.5 percent growth for 1997.
-- Snecma aircraft engine manufacturer to merge with its subsidiary SEP.
-- Thomson-CSF chairman Marcel Roulet hints at a decision on privatisation before the end of July.
-- Investment fund Northern Cross expected to vote in favour of the Eurotunnel financial restructuring prospectus.

-- Prime Minister Lionel Jospin criticised in his own Socialist-led parliamentary majority due to the rise in unemployment in May and his failure to prevent the shutdown of the Renault assembly plant in Vilvoorde, Belgium.
-- Competition battle among banks on consumer credit and housing credit is intensifying, competitive distortions include loss-making loans.
-- Bank Rothschild & Cie signs partnership agreement with U.S. group AIG on structured financing products.

-- Justice Minister Elisabeth Guigou says in an interview she rules out cutting links between the public prosecutor office and the chancellery, does not plan to reform law concerning the misappropriation of corporate funds.

-- Prime Minister Lionel Jospin may appear on television on Thursday to explain his policies in na "difficult" week marked by the Renault decision to go ahead with its Vilvoorde plant closure in Belgium.
-- The government is seeking a bidder for Thomson-CSF former subsidiary Thomainfor.
-- European Monetary Institute head Wim Duisenberg vows a 1999 start for European single currency.
